title: Ghosted Layers: Unconstrained Activation Alignment for Recovering Layer-Pruned LLMs
claim: Across existing recovery baselines, error stays high at the pruning boundary, while ours cuts it roughly in half.
layout: 1 panel, 7 vertical bars left-to-right, value labels, 'Ours' highlighted in red
description: A single bar chart on a light grey background showing boundary activation mean absolute error for seven methods. From left to right the bars are Pruned LLM (grey, 0.3916), LinearPatch D (orange, 0.4147), LinearPatch R (yellow, 0.4205), ReplaceMe LS (pale blue, 0.3772), ReplaceMe Cos (light green, 0.4752), Prune & Comp (blue, 0.4328), and Ours (dark red, 0.2151). Numeric values sit above each bar. The y-axis runs from 0.0 to about 0.5 with faint horizontal gridlines. The pastel baseline bars are all similar in height at roughly 0.38 to 0.48. The saturated red 'Ours' bar on the far right is much shorter and has a bold label, so the eye goes there first and sees a large drop in error.
caption: Boundary activation MAE on LLaMA-3.1-8B with 7 layers pruned by LLM-Streamline [ref], comparing existing recovery methods with Ghosted Layers.
abstract: Layer pruning removes entire Transformer decoder blocks from large language models, but introduces a mismatch between the hidden state received by the next surviving layer and the distribution it was trained to process, leading to significant performance degradation. We propose Ghosted Layers, a training-free recovery module that addresses this issue by solving a boundary activation alignment problem. Our method derives a closed-form optimal linear operator from a small calibration set to reconstruct the activation discrepancy introduced by the pruned layers. We show that this solution corresponds to the unconstrained optimum of the alignment objective, whereas LinearPatch is restricted to a fixed basis symmetric operator family. Across multiple LLM backbones, pruning strategies, and pruning depths, Ghosted Layers outperforms prior training-free recovery methods in accuracy and perplexity in most settings while preserving the efficiency benefits of layer pruning.
